site.name: greengrove
site.summary: greengrove-clone Fictional pet insurance "GreenGrove" marketing site, including a 6-step quote wizard. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Landing page: hand-drawn dog illustration hero + 3 value props + customer review cards + FAQ entry | | `quote.html` | 6-step quote wizard: 1 pet type (6 icon cards) / 2 breed (200+ dogs, 60+ cats, other species auto-switched ARIA combobox with searchable dropdown — keyboard up/down/Enter/Esc) / 3 age (year/month toggle + stepper) / 4 pre-existing conditions (19 chip multi-select + None toggle) / 5 three tier cards (Sprout / Sapling / Oak) + deductible dropdown + collapsible side-by-side comparison table + live per-tier quote / 6 quote summary (monthly fee + annual total + inclusions + 14-day price lock mock); top 6-step dot indicator allows jumping back; floating Back / Continue bar | | `faq.html` | 12 common-question `<details>` accordion |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full greengrove system, prioritizing the primary form/onboarding flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The GreenGrove website provides a generally clean interface, but suffers from a critical accessibility and usability blocker in its primary quote wizard. On mobile, the lack of a responsive navigation menu and small touch targets throughout the site introduce friction. The claims form handles data entry well with appropriate native HTML5 validation.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore the 6-step quote wizard, validate the claims submission form, and check FAQ interactions across desktop and mobile.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will start on the landing page to verify navigation, then dedicate the majority of effort to deeply exercising the 6-step quote wizard (especially the custom breed combobox and multi-select conditions). Afterward, it will validate the claims form and FAQ accordions. A final mobile pass will ensure the complex wizard UI and small tap targets remain usable on smaller screens.
assumptions: The 6-step quote wizard is contained within a single HTML file (quote.html) using JavaScript to manage state and DOM updates.
The breed combobox supports keyboard navigation (up/down/enter/esc) as described in the summary.
Form submissions (Claims) might be mocked but should have validation or success states.
risk_hotspots: quote.html: ARIA combobox for breed selection (keyboard navigation and dynamic filtering)
quote.html: State retention when navigating backward through the wizard steps
quote.html: Collapsible side-by-side comparison table on the Tier selection step
Header navigation: Multiple 'small_tap_target' warnings indicate potential mobile usability issues

key_checks: Open and close multiple <details> accordions on the FAQ page
exit_criteria: Successfully navigated to FAQ and toggled at least two questions.

phases.title: Quote Wizard - Steps 1-3
phases.objective: Exercise the initial data gathering steps of the quote flow.
key_checks: Interact with the breed combobox (type to filter, use arrow keys to select)
Use the age stepper and toggle between years/months
exit_criteria: Successfully progressed past the age step with valid data.

phases.title: Quote Wizard - Steps 4-6
phases.objective: Complete the quote flow, testing multi-select, tier cards, and summary.
key_checks: Select multiple pre-existing conditions and test the 'None' toggle
Select different coverage tiers and observe live quote updates
Use the dot indicator or 'Back' button to return to a previous step and verify state retention
Reach the final quote summary screen
exit_criteria: Final quote summary screen is reached and backward navigation was proven to retain state.

phases.objective: Validate the inputs and submission of the file a claim form.
key_checks: Fill out text, date, and number inputs
Interact with the file upload input

phases.title: Mobile Responsive Verification
phases.objective: Ensure complex components and small tap targets are usable on mobile.
key_checks: Complete a fast-path quote flow on the mobile viewport, focusing on the breed combobox and tier selection layout
exit_criteria: Completed one full quote flow in mobile mode.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise all 6 steps of the quote wizard, including edge cases like keyboard nav in combobox and 'None' toggle in conditions.
coverage_targets.mobile: Re-run the complete quote flow and test header navigation on mobile viewport.

notes: Pay special attention to the layout of the 6-step dot indicator and floating Back/Continue bar on mobile.

findings.problem: The pet type selection cards on Step 1 of the quote wizard are not keyboard accessible, are missing from the accessibility tree, and fail silently without an error message if the user clicks 'Continue' without making a selection.
findings.evidence: Agent logs state: 'Pressing Tab did not result in a visible focus on any of the custom pet selection cards' and 'Clicking Continue on Step 1... results in no action and provides no error message'.
findings.why_it_matters: Users relying on keyboards or screen readers cannot navigate or interact with the primary conversion funnel. Additionally, sighted users will be confused if they attempt to proceed without a selection and receive no feedback explaining why nothing happens.
findings.suggestion: Use semantic HTML (e.g., `<input type="radio">` visually hidden behind the cards, or `role="button"` with `tabindex="0"`) for the pet selection cards. Add explicit form validation that displays a clear error message (e.g., 'Please select a pet type') when proceeding without a selection.

findings.user_goal: Navigate the site and submit forms on a mobile device.
findings.problem: Interactive elements, including header navigation links and primary call-to-action buttons, are too small for comfortable and accurate touch interaction on mobile.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings flag the mobile header links ('Get a quote', 'Claims', 'FAQ') at 22-28px in height, and the 'Submit claim' / 'Continue' buttons at 39px in height, both of which fall below the standard 44px minimum touch target recommendation.
findings.why_it_matters: Small touch targets increase the likelihood of accidental misclicks, slowing down navigation and frustrating mobile users trying to complete tasks.
findings.suggestion: Increase the minimum height of primary buttons to at least 44px. For the mobile header, consider hiding the inline links behind a responsive hamburger menu, or increase their padding to ensure adequate spacing and touch target dimensions.
findings.source_hint: claims.html: Submit claim button / Header links

findings.problem: The 'Sign in' link in the landing page header acts as a dead link.
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'Sign in' button on the landing page header merely appends a hash ('#') to the URL without opening a modal or redirecting the user to an authentication page.
findings.why_it_matters: Returning customers looking to manage their policies or check claim statuses will hit a dead end, which can diminish trust in the platform.
findings.suggestion: Implement the sign-in functionality (e.g., redirect to a working login page or trigger a login modal), or remove the link entirely if the feature is not yet supported.
